clue.text: Hurt, still lying about America

indicators.note: lying about something means lying around it, so one piece wraps the other

parts.note: someone still lying down is in bed, abed
abbreviation for the United States

explanation.surface: An injured person is still lying in bed, perhaps after a fall somewhere in America.
explanation.definitionFit: Abused and hurt are both past participles describing someone who has been harmed or mistreated.

clue.text: Insect reported crawling up strongbox — take precautions!

indicators.note: something reported is passed on by word of mouth, so the sound counts, not the spelling

parts.note: a bee is an insect; the verb be sounds the same
an insect climbing a strongbox is on the side of the safe

explanation.surface: A bee is spotted climbing a safe, and someone shouts a warning to be careful.
explanation.walkthrough: Read literally, an insect crawling up a safe is on the safe's side; the idiom means play it safe.
explanation.definitionFit: The idiom 'be on the safe side' is a fixed phrase meaning act cautiously just in case, which matches the imperative.

clue.text: Old-fashioned duke raised to power

parts.note: a square is a conventional, old-fashioned person
D is the abbreviation for duke

explanation.surface: A stuffy, old-fashioned duke has been elevated to a position of power.
explanation.definitionFit: In arithmetic a number squared has been raised to the power of two, a mathematical sense of the phrase.

clue.text: Clothing in tatters, academic kept going for ages

indicators.note: clothing something means dressing it, so one piece is wrapped round the other

parts.note: a don is a university teacher
something in tatters is ragged

explanation.surface: A shabby academic in ragged clothes has been lecturing on and on for ages.
explanation.walkthrough: 'Clothing' looks like a noun for garments, but it is the verb: the don wraps around the ragged piece.
explanation.definitionFit: Something that dragged on continued tediously long, the phrasal verb in past tense matching kept going.

clue.text: Office lays claim to letters received

parts.note: a post is a position or office
to bag something is to claim it first, as children do

explanation.surface: A post office stakes its claim to the mail it has been sent.
explanation.walkthrough: 'Office' suggests a post office building, but it means a job or position.
explanation.definitionFit: A postbag is the mail an organisation or celebrity receives, so the plural covers the letters arriving.

clue.text: Bonus — rep's sick mum receives one

indicators.note: to receive something is to take it inside, so one piece goes within the rest
being sick suggests being out of sorts, so the letters are disordered

parts.note: taken as written
taken as written
the Roman numeral for one

explanation.surface: A salesman's mother is ill and gets a one-off bonus payment.
explanation.definitionFit: A premium is an extra sum paid on top of the usual amount, a synonym of bonus.

clue.text: Eg gravy dish with bottom missing

indicators.note: in a down entry the bottom is the final letter, and missing means it is dropped

parts.note: a saucer is a small dish

explanation.surface: A gravy boat has lost its base, leaving a mess.
explanation.definitionFit: Gravy is one example of a liquid served over food, which is what a sauce is.

clue.text: Country's short queen gets portable heater

indicators.note: short means cut off before the end, so the last letter of the country is lost

parts.note: the South American country
ER, Elizabeth Regina, is the usual crossword queen

explanation.surface: A small monarch of some nation is given a heater to carry about.
explanation.definitionFit: A brazier is a metal container holding burning coal, a movable source of warmth.

clue.text: Very successful crew given fish as parting gift

parts.note: a golden period is a very successful one
hands are crew members on a ship
hake is a sea fish

explanation.surface: A triumphant fishing crew is handed a fish as a farewell present.
explanation.definitionFit: A golden handshake is a large payment given to someone leaving a job, a generous farewell sum.

clue.text: Community site hosting university after work

indicators.note: a host takes guests in, so the other pieces sit inside the site

parts.note: a place is a site
op, short for opus, is a work
U is the abbreviation for university

explanation.surface: A local site hosts a university event after work for the neighbourhood.
explanation.definitionFit: The populace is the general population of a place, a synonym of the community living there.

clue.text: Posh fur fit for purpose

parts.note: U means upper-class, posh
sable is a costly fur

explanation.surface: An expensive, upper-class fur coat that is actually practical.
explanation.definitionFit: Usable means able to be used, which is what something fit for its purpose is.

clue.text: Leading renegades in the wrong direction

indicators.note: going the wrong way means the word is read back to front

parts.note: rats are deserters or traitors

explanation.surface: The chief turncoats are heading off the wrong way.
explanation.walkthrough: 'Leading' looks like it describes the renegades but is the definition, used as an adjective.
explanation.definitionFit: A star performer or star role is the leading one, the adjectival sense of the word.

clue.text: Courier reinforces instructions

parts.note: a courier is a tour guide
lining a garment strengthens it

explanation.surface: A delivery rider backs up the instructions they were given.
explanation.walkthrough: In British usage a courier is also a tour guide in charge of a holiday group.
explanation.definitionFit: Guidelines are rules or advice on how to do something, close in meaning to instructions.

clue.text: Former follower of fashion admits ambition to become cultivated

indicators.note: to admit is to let in, so one piece goes inside the other

parts.note: a Teddy boy, a 1950s British fashion follower
an end is an aim or goal

explanation.surface: An ex-trendsetter confesses a wish to become refined.
explanation.walkthrough: Teds were 1950s British youths in Edwardian-style suits; 'cultivated' looks like refined but means tilled or nurtured.
explanation.definitionFit: To cultivate plants is to tend them, so tended is the past tense of looking after a garden.

clue.text: Old knight needs cunning in my kingdom

indicators.note: in places the preceding pieces inside the last word

parts.note: taken as written
O is the abbreviation for old
N is the chess notation for a knight
arch means slyly knowing

explanation.surface: An elderly knight needs to be crafty to survive in this realm.
explanation.definitionFit: A monarchy is a state ruled by a king or queen, so a kingdom is one kind.

clue.text: State what pregnant cow might produce

definitions.meaning: first meaning: a state of the USA
second meaning: a fresh calf of a Channel Island dairy breed

explanation.walkthrough: 'State' looks like a verb meaning say, but it is a US state; Jersey is a breed of dairy cow, so its calf is a new one.
explanation.definitionFit: The American state is named after the Channel Island, and a newborn of that cattle breed would be a new one.

clue.text: Mother's always going on, losing head after morning's over

indicators.note: turned over means read the other way round

parts.note: a.m. denotes morning

indicators.note: losing its head means the first letter is cut off

parts.note: eternal means lasting for ever

explanation.surface: Mum is always going on and losing her temper once the morning is done.
explanation.walkthrough: 'Mother's' looks like a possessive noun but is the definition read as 'of a mother'.
explanation.definitionFit: Maternal is the adjective meaning belonging to or relating to a mother.

clue.text: Eager Conservative restrained by Left

indicators.note: something restrained is held in, so it goes inside the other piece

parts.note: left in the sense of went out
C is the abbreviation for Conservative

explanation.surface: A keen Tory is kept in check by the political Left.
explanation.walkthrough: 'Left' suggests the political wing, but it is the verb meaning departed.
explanation.definitionFit: Excited and eager both describe someone keenly looking forward to something, near synonyms.

clue.text: Article penned by tragic king of Morocco, possibly

indicators.note: something penned is shut in an enclosure, so it sits inside the other piece

parts.note: King Lear, Shakespeare's tragic hero
the definite article

explanation.surface: A tragic king writes an article, perhaps about Morocco.
explanation.walkthrough: Morocco looks like the country, but it is also a fine goatskin leather used in bookbinding.
explanation.definitionFit: Morocco is a kind of soft goatskin leather, so it is an example, flagged by possibly.

clue.text: Flourishing faction taking bible to heart

indicators.note: taking something in means holding it within, so one piece goes inside
to the heart means into the very middle, placing the inserted piece centrally

parts.note: a wing is a faction of a party
AV is the Authorised Version of the Bible

explanation.surface: A thriving religious group has taken scripture to heart.
explanation.walkthrough: 'Flourishing' suggests thriving, but here it means brandishing something in the air.
explanation.definitionFit: To flourish a flag or sword is to wave it about, so the participles match.

clue.text: Primarily, reason I've got dizzy?

indicators.note: dizzy means spinning and muddled, so the letters are jumbled
primarily means first of all, so only the opening letter is taken

parts.note: the first letter of reason
taken as written, apostrophe dropped

explanation.surface: Someone asks what is chiefly behind their dizzy spell.
explanation.walkthrough: The whole clue is both wordplay and definition: the condition is the main reason a person feels dizzy.
explanation.definitionFit: Vertigo is a medical sensation of spinning, the chief cause of feeling giddy.

clue.text: Holder used by schoolboy's pal: science freak

indicators.note: a freak is something abnormal, so these letters are twisted out of shape

parts.note: taken as written
taken as written

explanation.surface: A schoolboy's friend is a science nerd.
explanation.walkthrough: The 's after schoolboy stands for 'has': the definition, then has, then the wordplay.
explanation.definitionFit: A pencil case is a small container a pupil keeps pens and pencils in.

clue.text: Weapon carried by martial ancestors

indicators.note: carried by means held within, so the letters sit inside the following words

parts.note: the letters run from the end of the first word into the second

explanation.surface: A weapon wielded by warlike forebears.
explanation.definitionFit: A lance is a long spear carried by mounted knights, a type of weapon.

clue.text: Press losing initial feeling of euphoria

indicators.note: losing its initial means the first letter goes

parts.note: to crush is to press hard

explanation.surface: The newspapers lose their first sense of elation.
explanation.walkthrough: 'Press' suggests newspapers, but it is the verb meaning squeeze.
explanation.definitionFit: A rush is a sudden surge of excitement or pleasure, a sense of euphoria.

clue.text: Ex-boxer showing lean leg

parts.note: a ship lists when it leans
the leg side in cricket is the on side

explanation.surface: A former fighter shows off a skinny leg.
explanation.walkthrough: 'Lean' looks like thin, but it is the verb meaning tilt; in cricket the leg side is called the on side.
explanation.definitionFit: Sonny Liston was an American heavyweight champion of the 1960s, a retired fighter.

clue.text: Where pilot has received treatment?

indicators.note: being treated means being worked over, so the letters are reorganised

parts.note: taken as written

explanation.surface: Someone asks where an injured airman was treated.
explanation.walkthrough: The whole clue is the definition as well as the wordplay: a medical centre is where the pilot was cared for.
explanation.definitionFit: A hospital is the institution where patients are given medical care.

clue.text: Try to secure badly aged tiles

indicators.note: securing something means holding it fast inside

parts.note: a judge hears or tries a case

indicators.note: something done badly is messed up, so the letters are scrambled

parts.note: taken as written

explanation.surface: Someone attempts to fix some old, worn roof tiles.
explanation.walkthrough: 'Tiles' looks like roofing, but tile is old slang for a hat.
explanation.definitionFit: Tile is informal slang for a hat, so tiles are hats, collectively headgear.

clue.text: Old farmers longing to purchase 'ouse

indicators.note: purchasing something brings it in, so one piece goes inside the other

parts.note: a yen is a craving
dropping the H as in 'ouse, home becomes 'ome

explanation.surface: Traditional farmers yearn to buy a house, spoken with a dropped H.
explanation.walkthrough: 'Ouse is house with its H dropped, so the same accent turns home into 'ome.
explanation.definitionFit: Yeomen were historically small freeholding farmers who worked their own land in England.
